(Week 4) Shortcut Connections A shortcut connection allows information to skip over part of the network. Simple view: Input vector → processing layer → output vector With shortcut: Input vector → processing layer → add original input back → output vector Key idea: Shortcut connections help the model preserve useful information.
(Week 4) Shortcut Connections - Example Why Shortcut Connections Help Deep models can lose information as it passes through many layers. Shortcut connections help by: • preserving earlier information • improving gradient flow • making training more stable • helping very deep models learn Simple analogy: A shortcut path allows important information to travel more easily.
(Week 4) A shortcut connection adds the original input back after a processing layer: [1,2,3] + [0.2,-0.5,1.0] = [1.2,1.5,4.0]. It preserves earlier information, improves gradient flow and helps deep models train.
